Entry.CreatedBy: Codex Iriya lane C141-150 full-case author

Senses.PreferredTarget: the force of a thousand peaks stopping at the great mountain’s edge and the sound of myriad streams disappearing at the sea
SearchAliases: the force of a thousand peaks stopping at the great mountain’s edge and the sound of myriad streams disappearing at the sea
the convergence of a thousand peaks at the great mountain and myriad streams at the sea
Senses.Note: The couplet makes lesser heights and streams reach their limit at the great mountain and sea; it is retained as a paired convergence image.

ExplanationParts.CorpusEarnedOpening: Masters use the mountain-and-sea couplet after demands for a beyond-rank statement, in answers across traditions, and as a questioner’s advance that is sometimes dismissed as idle talk.
EvidenceBody: Both clauses recur together: peaks terminate at the great mountain and streams lose their sound at the sea, giving parallel land and water convergence.

DifferentThingTest.Reason: Both clauses recur together: peaks terminate at the great mountain and streams lose their sound at the sea, giving parallel land and water convergence.

DraftEvidence.AliasRationale: The English search form retains both mountain and sea clauses, matching the governed relation repeated in the reviewed cases.

ModifierControls.Finding: Either peaks or streams alone loses the couplet’s parallel convergence.

FamilyControls.Finding: Other landscape couplets do not count unless both limiting movements occur in parallel.
